summary: Baileys fork: keyword co-occurrence in utility module, no traced installer harm
details: @alannxd/baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web API library. A a static rule matched on keyword co-occurrence in lib/Utils/generics.js (tokens 'ping', 'GET', 'id') within a general-purpose utilities file. These tokens are consistent with the library's documented WhatsApp protocol handling (presence/ping frames, HTTP GET helpers, message identifiers) rather than exfiltration primitives. No hardcoded attacker C2 endpoint, no credential-path read (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc), no environment-variable scraping, no install-time or import-time execution of fetched code, no lifecycle scripts performing network I/O, and no dropper pattern are present in the evidence.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
